# Top-labelled text fields overlap the next row in CSS Grid

## Context

The State Provider demo renewal uses a grid for its top-labelled fields. Julia’s [PR #22028](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/22028) identified the shared field sizing bug and applies a local stylesheet workaround. I reproduced the shared behavior independently with the Engine checkout example’s shipping fields placed in a single-column CSS Grid with a 4 px gap.

## The Problem

At 1440 × 900 in Chromium, a regular top-labelled field is 27 px tall in Grid. Its input wrapper extends 19 px below the field, and the input box overlaps the following label by 6 px. Neo Light and Neo Dark reproduce the same geometry. In the checkout example’s original flex layout, the field measures 46 px and its wrapper fits.

## The Architectural Reality

`resources/css/src/form/field/Text.css` applies a single-line fixed height to `.neo-textfield`. The `.label-top` variant stacks the label and input vertically. Separate counter and in-flow error states already choose a content-sized grid. A correction to the base top-label height needs to preserve those states.

Design authority: `Neo.form.field.Text#labelPosition` supports a label above the input. The existing `.label-top` stylesheet places the label and input in a column.

## The Fix

Let the existing top-label variant use its intrinsic height in the shared stylesheet. Place the height adjustment before, and at equal specificity to, the later in-flow grid rule, so its `max-content` height still wins. Reuse the real field and grid layout in the component regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Two consecutive text fields with top labels in one grid column each contain their input, and the first input finishes above the second label.
- [ ] The existing top-label flex example, character-count state and in-flow error layouts still behave correctly.
- [ ] Verify the failure before the change and the corrected geometry in headless Chromium. Include the same checkout layout in Neo Light and Neo Dark.

## Out of Scope

Changing the State Provider example or its local workaround, changing input sizing tokens, or rearranging labels in other positions.

## Related

#21879, #22028, #21389. The last issue governs the in-flow error state and establishes the existing content-sized rule.

I’m taking the shared stylesheet and its component regression during the v14 release window.
